page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 32 GB of system RAM. Driven by dedicated AMD EPYC 9B45 processors running on the x86_64 architecture, the instance incorporates 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It lacks dedicated local storage and GPUs, requiring external storage volumes for stateful persistence. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic hardware extensions.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread efficiency, highlighted by top-tier ratings in stress-ng single-core (3423.37), Geekbench single-core (2522.0), single-threaded gzip compression (37.58 GB/sec), and bzip3 decompression (16.55 GB/sec). Conversely, aggregate throughput tests reflect the physical 2-core boundary, posting mid-tier results in multi-core stress-ng (6864.55), Geekbench multi-core (5758.0), and PassMark CPU (9142.2). Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth settles at 39.72 GB/sec with writes reaching 26.86 GB/sec.

Resource allocation delivers a high 1:8 core-to-memory ratio (8 GB RAM per vCPU), optimizing costs for footprints where thread concurrency is modest but in-memory working sets are substantial. The absence of local NVMe storage limits self-contained high-IOPS storage capabilities, and the configuration struggles with heavier AI tasks, as seen in the poor 14.83 tokens/sec prompt processing metric on 7B LLM models. It fits best with in-memory caching layers such as Redis, lightweight databases, memory-bound data transformations, and single-thread intensive backend services.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-4 is a memory-oriented virtual instance powered by AMD EPYC 9B45 processors on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs spanning 2 physical cores alongside 32 GB of RAM, offering a high 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports modern vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI, but does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier single-threaded compute and compression speeds, while multi-threaded capacity remains bounded within the middle tier by its 4-vCPU envelope. Delivering 7.4 million Redis SET operations per second and 14.48 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, the server exhibits strong cost efficiency for memory-intensive, low-parallelism workloads such as in-memory caches, small databases, and memory-heavy backend processing pipelines.
